candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On 'the Lord thy God will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, that thou mayest live' (Deu 30:6), Ephrem reads the heart-circumcision-by-divine-action as the canonical Old-Testament promise of grace fulfilled in the new covenant: what Deu 10:16 commands ('circumcise your heart'), Deu 30:6 promises the Lord himself will accomplish. The same gospel-of-grace structure (command becomes promise) flows through Jer 31:33 and Ez 36:26 into Acts 2's Pentecost. Tewahedo theosis-theology cites Deu 30:6 as the canonical Old-Testament anchor: the Spirit-given heart-circumcision IS theosis — God's own action transforming the human heart to love him with the love that he commands.

candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On 'the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it' (Deu 30:14), Ephrem reads the near-Word promise as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of Paul's exposition of the gospel-of-faith in Romans 10:8 ('The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach' — verbatim citation). The Deuteronomic word-near-to-you is appropriated by Paul as the gospel: salvation is not ascending to heaven (incarnation already happened) or descending to the abyss (resurrection already happened) but confessing with the mouth and believing with the heart. Tewahedo catechesis cites Deu 30:14 + Rom 10:8-10 as the canonical doubled-witness that the gospel is mouth-and-heart confession.
